title: Cybersecurity fundamentals
simple: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting people, devices, data, and services from harm.
technical: Study the CIA triad: confidentiality, integrity, and availability; then connect assets, threats, vulnerabilities, and controls.
quiz: Which CIA property means data is not changed without authorization?

title: Networking and web basics
simple: Devices use addresses and protocols to communicate, like houses use addresses and delivery rules.
technical: Explore IP addresses, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, cookies, clients, servers, and segmentation.
quiz: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?

title: Ethical hacking methodology
simple: Ethical hacking means testing only systems you are allowed to test, with a written scope.
technical: Use authorization, threat modeling, predefined test cases, evidence collection, and responsible reporting.
quiz: What must be defined before a security test?

title: Web application security
simple: Web apps must check what users are allowed to do and safely handle what they submit.
technical: Study access control, input validation, injection concepts, secure sessions, and the OWASP Top 10.

title: Defensive security
simple: Defenders make systems harder to misuse and easier to monitor.
technical: Practice secure configuration, logging, monitoring, segmentation, hardening, and incident response.
answer: They preserve evidence for detection and investigation

title: AI for cybersecurity
simple: AI can help explain evidence, but it can also be wrong or manipulated.
technical: Learn RAG, citations, prompt injection awareness, tool policies, structured output, and uncertainty.
quiz: Does retrieved text prove an agent is correct?

title: Security validation
simple: A defense is not proven by a confident sentence; it is checked against an expected result.
technical: Use reproducible test cases, assertions, regression checks, evidence IDs, and limitations.
quiz: Who should calculate pass or fail?

title: Advanced research track
simple: Research means asking careful questions and explaining what the evidence can and cannot show.
technical: Explore threat intelligence, secure agents, adversarial testing in a lab, and post-quantum security concepts.
quiz: What makes a research result credible?
answer: Reproducibility, evidence, limitations, and clear scope
